outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
Write
\[
f(x)=x^4-4x^3+0x^2+0x+6.
\]
Using the prime $2$, we have $2\nmid 1$, while $2$ divides every nonleading coefficient $-4,0,0,6$. Also, $4\nmid 6$. Therefore all hypotheses of Eisenstein's criterion are satisfied, so $f(x)$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.
\end{proof}
